research_updates.title: Construction audit — permits remain estimated administrative values
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Franklin assessor/property record, Inspection Services forms, Plan Commission and Common Council agendas/minutes, and archived city PDFs. Queries covered Expedient, MKE1, RagingWire, NTT, H-D Franklin, RDC-4777 Ironwood Drive LLC, 4777 W Ironwood, parcel 930-1001-000, PB22-0043, PB25-0303 and PM25-0174 for 2007-2026. The public record supports estimated permit values of $27,000, $580,190 and $250,132, but no invoice, contract, completion expenditure, equipment split, contractor payment, worker hour or payroll. PM25-0174 may overlap PB25-0303. A bounded PB25-0303-only construction-eligible allocation remains as a last-resort scope sensitivity; transferred job-year and local-purchase syntheses were removed rather than presented as Franklin activity.

source.title: City of Franklin linked property record - 4777 W Ironwood Drive
source.publisher: City of Franklin / Real Property Data
source.notes: Franklin's Assessor page links to this public property system. The current record labels the 26,428-square-foot, 2007 building as Expedient and identifies tax key 930-1001-000. The generated five-page report gives the 2026 land, improvement and total assessment, classifies the occupancy as a computer center, and lists dated building permits and reported amounts. The 2022 and 2025 alterations are post-opening permit records; amounts are not verified expenditures and are not summed here.

research_updates.title: Operations audit — capacity is observed, realized Franklin employment is not
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Expedient's October 20, 2021 opening release, current MKE1/IRN specification and knowledge-base pages, 2021-2026 press archives, ESG pages and current careers index. Queries used Expedient, MKE1, IRN, Milwaukee, Franklin, 4777 Ironwood, jobs, payroll and employees. Dated facility area and critical-load specifications are retained. The 2021 plan to hire twelve remains a forecast. The current careers page showed one Milwaukee-market Regional Account Executive vacancy, not a filled MKE1 operations job. No site FTE, payroll, wage, occupied rack, revenue or operating-expense observation was found.

source.title: Expedient job listings — Milwaukee market
source.notes: The current careers index returned one Milwaukee-market opening, Regional Account Executive. A vacancy is neither a filled position nor necessarily based at MKE1; the listing supplies no Franklin-site headcount, payroll, hours, residence or realization of the 2021 twelve-hire plan.

research_updates.title: Fiscal audit — five parcel-tax principals verified; no listed state data-center exemption
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Milwaukee County Treasurer parcel account 9301001000, bills 289047, 314923, 353779, 366879 and 380021 for tax years 2021-2025; Franklin assessment rolls; Wisconsin DOR qualified-data-center guidance and certified-center list; WEDC program and transparency pages; and DFI entity search for the parcel owner. The five principal amounts are normalized separately from interest and penalties. DOR's list current through October 31, 2025 contains four certified projects and no Expedient, MKE1, Franklin site or RDC-4777 entity. No personal-property tax, sales-tax benefit, state award, operator reimbursement or same-scope net fiscal result was found.

source.title: Wisconsin DOR Qualified Data Center Exemption — certified centers
source.notes: The official list, current through October 31, 2025, names Microsoft, Epic Hosting, Degas and Oracle/Green Chile only. Expedient, MKE1, RDC-4777 Ironwood Drive LLC, Franklin and parcel 9301001000 do not appear; no qualified-data-center exemption is recorded for this property in the list.

research_updates.title: Community audit — no Milwaukee or Franklin transfer was disclosed
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Expedient press archives, current ESG/community pages, MKE Tech Hub references and searches for Milwaukee/Franklin donation, grant, volunteer, school, nonprofit and recipient disclosures from 2020-2026. A $100,000 national Feeding America donation predates the MKE1 opening and its named recipient list excludes Milwaukee and Franklin; it is not allocated here. Current pages describe volunteering and school partnerships only in general terms. No MKE1 recipient, cash amount, in-kind value or volunteer-hour quantity was found, so the prior induced-household-output synthesis was removed and no community benefit is inferred.

source.title: Expedient Announces Commitment to Communities during COVID-19
source.notes: The release reports a $100,000 national Feeding America donation before the Milwaukee site opened and lists recipient food banks in then-current data-center communities; no Milwaukee or Franklin recipient is listed. The amount is not allocated to this project.

research_updates.title: Investment audit — property transfer and lease terms remain distinct from new capital formation
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: archived Franklin Resolution 2012-6791 and CSM 8452 parcel history; Milwaukee County assessment, tax and Register of Deeds access pages; Wisconsin DFI; StratCap's August 10, 2022 buyer release; SEC searches; and contemporaneous local reporting. Queries used 4777 W Ironwood, tax key 930-1001-000, RDC-4777 Ironwood Drive LLC, Expedient, RagingWire, NTT and H-D Franklin for 2007-2026. The buyer release confirms a fully leased triple-net property with about fifteen years remaining, 2.5% escalators and renewal options, while only the secondary report supplies the $9.46 million price. No deed instrument, mortgage amount, rent, Expedient tenant-improvement cost, IT-equipment investment or locally retained capital was public.

source.title: StratCap Acquires Milwaukee Data Center
source.publisher: StratCap via Institutional Real Estate, Inc.
source.notes: The buyer's release identifies a 28,500-square-foot, 2.64-acre Franklin data center fully leased to Expedient on a triple-net basis, with about 15 years remaining, 2.5% annual escalators and three three-year renewal options. It does not disclose purchase price, rent, financing, tenant-improvement spending or local procurement.

research_updates.title: Public-cost audit — zero parcel special assessment is not zero service cost
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: the 2025 county tax account's special-assessment and special-charge rows; Franklin Common Council/Plan Commission archives and water/sewer permit materials; Milwaukee County budgets and deed access; and PSC utility-construction and water-regulation guidance for 2021-2026. Searches used the address, parcel, operator and owner names. The 2025 parcel page reports $0 special assessments and $0 special charges, but that does not measure police, fire, road, administrative, utility or financing cost. No project-attributable public expenditure was found. Only the exact tax-equal cost threshold is retained; no actual cost or fiscal net is asserted.

source.title: The Public Service Commission and Data Centers
source.notes: PSC states that it does not permit or directly regulate data-center construction or operations and does not track individual business water consumption. PSC and utility searches for Expedient, MKE1, 4777 Ironwood and parcel 9301001000 found no site-specific utility docket, meter, bill, tariff allocation or water record for 2021-2026.

research_updates.title: Resource audit — company goals do not supply MKE1 meter data
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Expedient's 2022 GRESB release, 2025 ESG/sustainability and objective pages, current MKE1 specification, PSC docket and guidance pages, We Energies data-center and tariff pages, and Franklin water/sewer materials. Queries covered Expedient, MKE1, 4777 Ironwood, electricity, PUE, water, wastewater, emissions, renewable energy and meter for 2021-2026. The operator reports a 1.6 MW critical-load capacity and company-wide monitoring and renewable goals, but no MKE1 utilization, PUE, kWh, peak demand, water, sewer, emissions or renewable share. PSC states it does not track individual-business water use. The capacity-based utilization/PUE range is retained only as a last-resort engineering sensitivity and not as observed consumption.

source.title: Environmental, Social, and Governance Practices
source.notes: The operator describes company-wide energy monitoring, cooling optimization, renewable-energy goals, volunteer opportunities and school partnerships. It supplies no MKE1-specific electricity, PUE, water, wastewater, emissions, renewable share, volunteer hours, recipient or transfer amount.

research_updates.title: Supplier audit — one carrier relationship is identifiable, procurement value is not
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Franklin permit/property records for contractor fields; Expedient MKE1 specifications and technology-partner pages; carrier-location directories; acquisition materials; and searches for procurement, vendor, supplier, contract and payment disclosures from 2021-2026. The current operator page reports four on-net carriers and Cogent independently lists MKE1 at 4777 Ironwood, but public sources disclose no price, payment, contractor identity for the cited permits, supplier geography or Milwaukee County retained share. The local-construction-spend and operating-supplier-output syntheses were removed.

source.title: Cogent service locations — Milwaukee metro
source.notes: Cogent identifies Expedient MKE1 at 4777 Ironwood Drive as a carrier-neutral data-center service location. This confirms one provider relationship but discloses no contract, payment, local supplier address, procurement amount or retained share.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective public-source audit for Microsoft's data-center property at 5150 Rogers Road and explicitly labeled wider Microsoft/Bexar County activity. Exact-site ordinance, permit, appraisal, and tax-account records remain separate from later campuses and regional disclosures; the three appraisal accounts and two taxable-account payments are not consolidated. Permit value is administrative, the original investment and employment figures are commitments, the 2013 employment threshold is a reported lower bound, and the water quantity is a projection rather than metered consumption. No Bexar-and-Medina total is allocated to this property. Annual construction expenditure, construction labor and residence, supplier payments, operating payroll and purchases, recipient-level tax distributions, marginal public-service cost, electricity consumption, water withdrawal or consumption, wastewater, actual emissions, and a recurring facility-level community series remain unobserved after the documented searches. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 evidence audit. Official parcel, permit, tax, water-account, state-certificate, EPA and operator records are retained as direct observations or clearly labeled source forecasts. Conflicting floor-area figures remain separate because their reporting definitions differ. Construction cost, realized jobs, supplier payments, community funding, electricity, emissions, wastewater, actual public-service cost and causal county effects remain unbounded rather than being filled with transferred assumptions. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective primary-source audit adds current Andale parcel assessment, contractor-reported campus floor area, and two recipient- or government-reported Meta community grants. The search trail records useful and negative results across identity, tax, construction, jobs, suppliers, utilities, water, permits, public costs, incentives, community funding, and county comparison inputs. Campus-wide facts remain unallocated to the selected inventory building, overlapping community amounts are not added together, and unavailable supplier, payroll, utility-billing, discharge, generator, and marginal-service-cost amounts remain explicit gaps. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Apple's Washoe County data-center campus at 21505 Reno Technology Parkway West and its 2024 expansion application. GOED audit findings, application forecasts, county permit values, parcel assessments, a water-right allocation, operator-reported electricity use, and recipient-reported donation bands remain separate evidence states and scopes. Permit values are administrative amounts and are not summed because overlapping scopes cannot be ruled out. Assessment values are parcel stocks, not investment or tax receipts. The 125 acre-foot water right is regulatory capacity, not measured use. Food Bank gifts are company-region transfers, not campus-attributable annual spending. No campus total is allocated to the selected mapped building; the four-building campus, later buildout cases, downtown Reno warehouse, supporting renewable projects, fire-station parcel, and more-than-200-person support statement are not collapsed into one footprint. No Switch Citadel or Storey County amount enters this fragment. Vendor payments, worker residence, taxes received by jurisdiction, realized 2024 abatement, same-scope public-service cost, wastewater, and building-level electricity or water remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Expedient's adaptive reuse of the pre-existing data-center building at 4777 W Ironwood Drive. The review searched Franklin planning, agenda, assessment, permit, water and sewer materials; Milwaukee County tax and deed-record access points; Wisconsin DOR, WEDC, DFI and PSC records; operator press, specification, career, ESG and community pages; lease, financing, carrier and vendor disclosures; and archived official pages for 2007-2026. Opening-day and current operator specifications remain separate dated snapshots because the reported area and capacity changed. The county portal now establishes a 2021-2025 parcel-tax principal series, but not Expedient's incidence under the lease. The 2022 ownership transfer, assessments, estimated permit values, tax payments and hiring plan remain non-additive. No source was found for actual construction outlays, realized site employment or payroll, local procurement, Milwaukee-area community transfers, metered resources, project-attributable public costs or a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Google's Council Bluffs data-center activity, retaining the selected inventory building as the project key while leaving campus, taxpayer-account, company-county, and state-award facts at their reported scopes. The audit distinguishes completed IEDA contracts 08-HQJC-030 and 12-HQJP-051 from the 2022 award still in performance; permit valuations remain administrative amounts rather than expenditure; assessed and taxable values remain stocks; bills remain distinct from payments; and community grants remain recipient- and period-specific. No value is inferred for sales-tax exemptions, the local abatement schedule, franchise-fee adjustment, electricity, supplier retention, building-level water, marginal public-service cost, or net fiscal position. Models without defensible project allocation or transferable parameters were removed even though that leaves the eight-category account incomplete.

modeled_scope_note: Modeled contribution accounts for Apple Mesa / Maricopa County, Switch Citadel / Storey County, and Digital Crossroad Hammond / Lake County. Every required account category and county-comparison module contains sourced evidence or a visibly labeled modeled value. Public support is not netted against unmatched local revenues, unavailable public-service cost is represented by a break-even threshold rather than an invented net margin, county comparisons are descriptive rather than causal, and low-confidence transferred benchmarks remain explicit. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution.

project_description: Expedient MKE1 is a colocation data center operated by Expedient at 4777 W Ironwood Drive in Franklin, Milwaukee County, Wisconsin. This project account covers the single adaptive-reuse facility and its parcel, not Expedient's wider regional portfolio, and keeps the October 2021 opening snapshot separate from later current specifications. Public records trace the pre-existing building, leased operation, 2022 ownership transfer, and subsequent facility permits.
